featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!

•	Chettinad prawn biryani: Spicy, aromatic, and generously portioned for a satisfying coastal twist.
Vibe and Service

featured_reviews.name: Yogen Sachdev
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally revisited Maaslli – Saraswat and GSB Speciality last night for my annual catch-up with friends, and once again, it reminded me why this place is rightly awarded the best seafood restaurant in Mumbai.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back.

featured_reviews.name: NOSHIR KATRAK
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maaslli Restaurant & Bar, at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Basically a Sea food Restaurant, but also have other non veg dishes on their platter.
One cannot afford to miss the fried Bombil (Fresh, Fried Bombay Ducks).
They have a great Menu.
They do have various Thali dishes and other alcarte dishes.
It is just mouth watering and thus unable to put in words to describe the dishes.
One must enjoy the crab dishes and crab soup.
They also present you their fresh catch and you may select the fish if your choice, depending upon the weight the rate is fixed.
The atmosphere is damn cool and decent with fishes reflecting in the walls and partisans.
The curry, different types is served and we are asked to taste, then by adding coconut oil again to try. Thus if you are ordering any curry dish you can select your choice of curry.
The staff is very courteous and friendly.
The person, Mr. Anthony, accepting the order is very polite and well versed with the description of the dishes.
Service is quite fast and dishes are very tempting.
The complete crockery is if copper OR may be brass (not sure). But it is a real experience to have your food in such dish and even the fork and spoon.
The soup was something different from the normal ones which all must have experienced.
Crab soup, very tasty and hot enough and goes without saying very tasty.
Sweet dish of Modak and a sweetening dish made if milk and sprinkled with pista, woh! Lovely.
The dishes are well place and economically rated.
If you are in that area, do give a try and taste the tasty dishes, yes! Definitely one have a inclination and a taste for Sea Food.
The Bar is open and you have choices of hard drinks, Cocktails and even Mocktails.
A seperate Menu displaying the drinks is maintained.
Do visit, you will not regret nor your pockets will be pinched.
Enjoy the Sea Food and friendly service.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text: This unassuming spot might just serve some of the best fried prawns in the city. The tiny interiors and no-frills ambiance could easily mislead a first-time visitor, but the food quickly sets the record straight. The prawns are succulent and perfectly cooked, encased in a crisp, red coloured batter that achieves just the right balance of texture and flavour. The accompanying green chutney is a standout, adding a zesty punch that elevates the dish to another level. featured_reviews.name: Daddyslittlelunchbox

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

Just experienced a fantastic meal at the iconic Bharat Excellensea, a 35-year-old gem in Mumbai's Ballard Estate! The restaurant has been recently revamped, and the ambiance is now even more inviting. But the real star is the food!

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Danish Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food Review: A Major Disappointment
​I truly believe one shouldn't speak ill of food, but I had an absolutely terrible experience here.
​We ordered the Prawns Koliwada and Crispy Chicken. Given the massive hype surrounding this restaurant, we expected the food to be exceptional. As a seafood lover—especially prawns fry—I was genuinely shocked from the very first bite. The Prawns Koliwada was completely tasteless; the spice profile was missing and there was no salt at all.
​To make matters worse, when my wife cut into a prawn, we realized they hadn't been cleaned properly. The digestive tracks (veins) were still inside. Every single prawn was like that, which completely ruined our appetite. On top of that, the dish was incredibly expensive.

​The Crispy Chicken
​The second dish was just as bad. It was so sour that after just one bite, we had to ask the waiter to pack it up. Neither my wife nor my kids could eat it—it was a total waste of money. I’ve had Crispy Chicken at many places, but this was the worst. Honestly, the local Chinese joint in my neighborhood makes it better.

​The Lesson Learned
​This experience taught me one thing: don't just rush to a restaurant based on an influencer's video. You have to check real reviews first. I have no idea what people actually like about the food there. My wife and I are beyond disappointed.

*1/5 — Extremely disappointing*

What went wrong:
- Taste: Bland and lacked the rich, aromatic flavor you expect from biryani. The masala tasted undercooked and oily.

-Rice: Overcooked and clumped together. No fragrance of saffron, kewra, or whole spices. -Overall quality: Greasy, heavy, and left an unpleasant aftertaste.

Would not recommend and won’t order again. If you’re craving biryani, better to skip this one.

featured_reviews.review_text: I can't put in words how much I appreciate this humble family owned place being where it is, offering God honest tasty Maharashtrian food at honest to God prices. The stars don't do real justice to this place because rating in stars is comparison with other places, and there isn't anything like this place around. featured_reviews.name: nigel faleiro
featured_reviews.review_text:

Seeing the prices on the menu I was wondering if the food or quantity would be any good but I was wrong. The size of the chapatis were bigger than most other expensive places, had a good number of meaty chicken pieces and very less bones 👌🏻

customer_updates.text: 10 / 10 for all the food we ordered. The dim sums and sushis are a melt in the mouth. Garlic edamame fried rice and pan fried hakka noodles were a Wow. Will definetely say this is may favourite Chinese restaurant in mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Ishita Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this restaurant during our outing to Marine Drive. The location is great if you’re around the area, but the overall experience was mixed.

One major issue was parking — it was quite difficult to find a spot nearby. There was also a long queue, so be prepared for a waiting time, especially during peak hours.

Coming to the food:

Foo Bao (Mushroom & Pepper) – 5/5 🌟
Definitely the best dish we tried. The flavors were on point and well balanced.

Shishito Charcoal Tempura Uramaki – 3/5
It was decent but nothing very memorable.

Pan-Fried Noodles – 1/5
This was disappointing and lacked flavor.

Overall, the food was average except for the Foo Bao, which really stood out.

Food: 3/5
Service: 3/5
Ambience: 3/5

Would visit again only for the Foo Bao.

featured_reviews.name: Sneha Chaturvedi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Foo Town for dinner with my mum and had a great experience. The moment we walked in, the ambience stood out straight away! the lighting, decor, and overall atmosphere were beautiful and made the place feel really special.

The drinks were amazing as well, and the staff were all incredibly sweet and welcoming throughout the evening. The only issue we had was with one dish we ordered that never arrived. We asked about it twice and were told they would check on it, but it still didn’t come, so we ended up ordering another plate of sushi while we waited.

Thankfully, the missing dish wasn’t added to our bill, so no complaints there. It was a small hiccup, and I’d just suggest being a bit more mindful with orders, but apart from that everything was lovely.

The food we did receive was great, the atmosphere was stunning, and overall it was a really enjoyable dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
The first thing to notice is comfortable booth seating, if you are lucky to get one of those spaces. Higher partitions provide good privacy between tables.

As expected, wide selection of drinks, including rice beer on tap.

Lotus stem bites were the only vegetarian option in our otherwise carnivore heavy selection...pork, tenderloin, prawns, crab meat, hamachi. Supremely satisfying.

Oh yes, and the famous blue rice - tenderly flavoured with a really quite special texture, easygoing on the palate, complimenting the rest of our food.

Wait staff tried pushing the Mount Foo-ji desert, but we opted for mango pudding and a hazelnut sweet instead.

There was a queue when we left after 10 pm, confirming the restaurant's popularity.

featured_reviews.review_text:

I think we should have stick to blue rice and green thai curry

Loved chatting with him.

Can try but seating is a problem on the weekends.
